docs.title: AI Service
docs.text: KNode uses Gemini for three jobs: reading organisation information, reading funding calls, and checking evidence against requirements. Everything else, including scores and eligibility, is calculated by fixed rules.

docs.title: Where AI is used
docs.text:
Entry point Trigger What it does services/jobs/scraper.py Background job Finds an organisation's website and extracts its profile services/jobs/midnight_scraper.py Scheduled job (10 organisations per run) Finds an organisation's website and extracts its profile, in small batches services/jobs/process_grants.py Background job Extracts structured requirements from stored grants (50 per run) services/jobs/midnight_grants.py Scheduled job (10 grants per run) Pulls Africa-related grants from Grants.gov and extracts them POST /opportunities/extract Funder or admin uploads a file Returns a draft opportunity for review POST /organisations/{id}/documents User uploads a document Extracts profile facts into PENDING claims Matching engine Match request Checks evidence against each requirement (off by default)

The model is set by GEMINI_MODEL (default gemini-3.8-flash). Every call needs GEMINI_API_KEY.

docs.title: Calling Gemini
docs.text:
The backend makes three kinds of call. All three ask for JSON back.

Client setupExtract from textExtract from a fileAssess a requirement

services/ai_service.py builds one shared client. It uses an API key if present, and otherwise Vertex AI.

from google import genai

def _build_client():
    if settings.GEMINI_API_KEY:
        return genai.Client(api_key=settings.GEMINI_API_KEY)
    if settings.GCP_PROJECT_ID:
        return genai.Client(
            vertexai=True,
            project=settings.GCP_PROJECT_ID,
            location=settings.GCP_REGION,
        )
    return None

client = _build_client()

Used for website text and funding calls. The response is forced into a Pydantic schema, and the temperature is low so results are stable.

from google.genai import types

response = client.models.generate_content(
    model=settings.GEMINI_MODEL,
    contents=prompt,
    config=types.GenerateContentConfig(
        response_mime_type="application/json",
        response_schema=ExtractedEvidence,
        temperature=0.1,
    ),
)
data = json.loads(response.text)

The scraped text goes inside <untrusted_text> tags, and the prompt tells the model to ignore any instructions found there.

services/document_extraction.py sends the uploaded PDF, image or text directly to Gemini and validates the reply against a schema.

client = genai.Client(api_key=settings.GEMINI_API_KEY)
interaction = client.interactions.create(
    model=settings.GEMINI_MODEL,
    input=_input_items(kind, data),
    response_format={
        "type": "text",
        "mime_type": "application/json",
        "schema": ExtractedProfile.model_json_schema(),
    },
)
profile = ExtractedProfile.model_validate_json(interaction.output_text)

If the reply fails validation, the upload is rejected and nothing is saved.

services/matching_engine/gemini_provider.py uses temperature 0 and a separate system instruction. It also sets a timeout.

class GenAIJsonGenerator:
    def __init__(self, api_key, model, timeout_seconds=30):
        from google import genai
        from google.genai import types

        self._types = types
        self._model = model
        self._client = genai.Client(
            api_key=api_key,
            http_options=types.HttpOptions(timeout=int(timeout_seconds * 1000)),
        )

    def generate(self, system, user):
        response = self._client.models.generate_content(
            model=self._model,
            contents=user,
            config=self._types.GenerateContentConfig(
                system_instruction=system,
                temperature=0.0,
                response_mime_type="application/json",
            ),
        )
        return response.text

docs.title: 1. Organisation extraction
docs.text:
From a websiteFrom an uploaded document

Code: jobs/scraper.py, jobs/midnight_scraper.py

  1. Organisations are loaded from the IRS tax-exempt file (up to 100 per run; health, livelihoods and Africa-related names).
  2. A Serper search finds the official website (social media and directory sites are skipped).
  3. The page is scraped. If it has under 200 characters, the website is discarded.
  4. Gemini extracts the mission, capabilities, countries and focus areas.
  5. If both a mission and capabilities came back, they are saved onto the organisation.
  6. The job waits 4 seconds between organisations.

No review step on this path

Website results are written directly onto the organisation record. They do not create PENDING claims or a source record.

Endpoint: POST /organisations/{organisation_id}/documents (multipart form, field file)

  • Accepts PDF, PNG and DOCX. DOCX is converted to text first.
  • Each fact becomes a PENDING claim linked to a source record.
  • The response returns source_id, fields_updated, claims_added and the updated organisation.
  • A person moves each claim to CONFIRMED or DISPUTED. Only CONFIRMED claims are used in matching.

Prompt rules: extract only what is explicitly stated, focus area must be HEALTH or LIVELIHOODS, and countries must be African.

Cleaning: HTML is stripped and lengths are capped (mission 200 characters, 10 capabilities, 15 countries). Any error returns an empty result, so a failed call never invents data.

From tests/test_ai_pipeline.py, for the text "We provide clean water in Kenya.":

{
  "mission": "To provide clean water.",
  "capabilities": ["WASH"],
  "countries_of_operation": ["Kenya"],
  "focus_areas": ["HEALTH"]
}

docs.title: 2. Opportunity extraction
docs.text:
From Grants.govFrom stored grantsFrom an uploaded file

Code: jobs/midnight_grants.py

  1. Searches the Grants.gov API for the keyword Africa, posted in the last 60 days (20 rows).
  2. Skips any grant already stored.
  3. Fetches the grant's description and sends it to Gemini.
  4. Saves it only if Gemini returned a title and at least one requirement.
  5. Creates the funder if it does not exist yet, then the opportunity and each requirement.
  6. Saved with source GRANTS_GOV, status OPEN and currency USD.

Code: jobs/process_grants.py

Processes up to 50 grants per run, 7 seconds apart. Opportunities that have a description but no requirements yet are extracted and updated.

Endpoint: POST /opportunities/extract (funder or admin only)

Accepts a PDF, DOCX or TXT up to 10 MB and returns a draft opportunity. Nothing is saved until the funder reviews it and creates the opportunity.

The model returns no title, which rejects the call, when it is for a non-African region, is not an open call organisations can apply to, or is already past its deadline. Amounts are copied as written and never converted. With no currency stated, both amounts are set to null. At most 30 requirements are kept, each with a type (eligibility, geography, thematic_fit, financial_capacity, partnership or evidence).

From tests/test_opportunity_extract.py:

docs.title: 3. Requirement assessment
docs.text:
Code: matching_engine/gemini_provider.py, assessment.py

Turned on with AI_ASSESSMENT_ENABLED=true. For one requirement, the system finds up to 5 of the organisation's CONFIRMED claims by keyword overlap and asks Gemini for a verdict. If nothing overlaps, no call is made and the result is UNKNOWN.

The prompt built for the requirement youth digital skills programme:

<<<REQUIREMENT
youth digital skills programme
REQUIREMENT>>>

<<<EVIDENCE P1
We delivered a youth digital skills programme across Kenya in 2024. Contact: [email removed]
EVIDENCE>>>

The reply Gemini must give:

{
  "status": "MET",
  "passage": "P1",
  "quote": "youth digital skills programme",
  "reasoning": "The passage states the programme was delivered."
}

Safeguards

  • Possible statuses: MET, PARTIALLY_MET, NOT_MET, UNKNOWN. Unclear or missing evidence is UNKNOWN, never NOT_MET.
  • The quote must appear in the cited passage. If not, the result becomes UNKNOWN and is flagged for review.
  • Database IDs never reach the model, emails are masked, and <<< and >>> are removed from evidence.
  • A failed call is retried up to 2 times. If it still fails, the result is ERROR, which is not counted as a finding.

docs.title: How a match is scored
docs.text:
Four steps. Only step 2 uses AI.

  1. Eligibility (rules): deadline not passed, geography overlap, organisation type.
  2. Assessment (AI, optional): each requirement gets a status.
  3. Score (rules): weighted by category, out of 100.
  4. Explanation (template): built from the score and its breakdown.
Eligibility rules Condition Result Deadline passed FAILED Deadline not passed SATISFIED Geography overlaps the organisation's countries SATISFIED No geography overlap UNKNOWN (not a failure) Opportunity lists organisation types UNKNOWN (not yet checked) 
Overall: `INELIGIBLE` if any condition failed, `ELIGIBLE` if all are satisfied, otherwise `NEEDS_VERIFICATION`.
Score weights (match-score-v1)

MET counts 4, PARTIALLY_MET counts 2, NOT_MET counts 0, out of 4.

| Category | Weight |
|---|---|
| Programme strategic alignment | 25% |
| Programme delivery capability | 25% |
| Experience and track record | 20% |
| Target population and context | 15% |
| Team capacity | 15% |

Unassessed requirements (`UNKNOWN`, `NOT_CHECKED`, `ERROR`) are left out of the score and lower the **evidence coverage**. Score status is `COMPLETE`, `PROVISIONAL` or `NOT_CALCULABLE`. If the funding call publishes its own weights, those replace the defaults.

docs.title: Worked example
docs.text:
Five requirements, one per category. Four are assessed, one has no evidence.

Category Status Weight Contribution Programme strategic alignment MET 0.25 0.250 Programme delivery capability PARTIALLY_MET 0.25 0.125 Experience and track record MET 0.20 0.200 Target population and context UNKNOWN 0.15 not scored Team capacity MET 0.15 0.150 
(0.250 + 0.125 + 0.200 + 0.150) / 0.85 × 100 = 85.3

Result: score 85.3, status PROVISIONAL, evidence coverage 85%. The unknown requirement is left out, not counted as a failure. The same inputs always give the same score.

docs.title: Guardrails
docs.text:
These controls apply to the AI itself: what goes into the model, what comes out, and what it is allowed to do.

Before the modelAfter the modelHuman oversightWhen the AI fails
  • Scraped text, documents and evidence are wrapped in markers and labelled as untrusted. The model is told to ignore any instructions inside them.
  • Any marker text found inside the input is removed first, so content cannot close the block early.
  • Text sent for extraction is cut to AI_MAX_TEXT_LENGTH (20,000 characters).
  • Assessment prompts contain no database IDs and no organisation names. Evidence passages are labelled P1, P2 and so on, and mapped back afterwards.
  • Email addresses in evidence are replaced with [email removed].
  • Prompts tell the model not to guess. Missing information must be left out.
  • Assessment runs at temperature 0 and extraction at 0.1, so results stay stable.
Check Behaviour Forced schema Replies must be JSON matching a Pydantic schema. A reply that fails validation is rejected and nothing is saved. Field limits Mission 5,000 characters, up to 30 capabilities, 60 countries, 12 impact metrics, 20 other facts Number checks Annual revenue cannot be negative. Currency must be three capital letters. Allowed values Focus areas are limited to HEALTH and LIVELIHOODS. Other values are dropped. HTML Tags are stripped from every text field Quotes An assessment must quote the passage it cites. If the quote is not in that passage, the result becomes UNKNOWN and is flagged for review. No evidence, no verdict An assessed status with no evidence reference is downgraded to UNKNOWN. Unclear evidence Treated as UNKNOWN, never NOT_MET. NOT_MET needs a passage that contradicts the requirement. Grant checks A call with no title is rejected. Past deadlines, non-African regions and non-open calls are rejected. Money Amounts are copied as written. Nothing is converted or guessed.
  • Facts the AI extracts from uploaded documents are saved as PENDING claims. A person must confirm or dispute each one.
  • Only CONFIRMED claims are used as evidence when the AI assesses a requirement.
  • A funding call extracted from an upload comes back as a draft. Nothing is saved until the funder reviews and submits it.
  • The AI does not write the match explanation or calculate the score. Both come from fixed rules, so they cannot contain claims the AI made up.
  • Assessment is switched off by default and must be enabled with AI_ASSESSMENT_ENABLED.
Situation What happens No API key Document extraction returns 503 (AI_NOT_CONFIGURED). Assessment is skipped. Call fails or times out Document extraction returns 502 (EXTRACTION_FAILED). Assessment is retried up to 2 times with backoff, then recorded as ERROR. Reply is invalid Rejected. No data is saved. Website extraction returns nothing usable The website is discarded and no organisation fields are changed Logging Only the error type is logged, not the document content

An assessment ERROR is not counted as a finding about the organisation. It is left out of the score and lowers the evidence coverage.

What the AI must never do

  • Decide who receives funding
  • Verify an organisation on its own
  • Declare an organisation legitimate without evidence
  • Approve organisations or form binding partnerships
  • Make legal decisions
  • Guarantee that an organisation will qualify for or win a grant
  • Replace funder due diligence

docs.title: KNode Technical Architecture & AI Integration
docs.text:
Status and evidence

This page describes KNode's target architecture together with its current implementation status. Each component and control carries a label:

Label Meaning Implemented Found in code (alya-backend or alya-frontend-develop) Partial Exists but incomplete or not verified on every route Planned Design target; not present in the code reviewed

Evidence checked: alya-backend @ <commit-sha> (main.py, core/config.py, core/security.py, core/dependencies.py, database.py) and alya-frontend-develop @ <commit-sha>. Last reviewed: 26 Oct 2026. A summary of every control is in Section 11.

docs.title: 1. Architecture Overview
docs.text: KNode is a single application with separate background processing. Users work in dashboards for NGOs, funders and administrators, which send requests to a central interface that checks identity and permissions. The interface is divided into self-contained modules, such as authentication, verification, matching and reports. Slow tasks, such as collecting data, reading documents and running AI extraction, are designed to be queued and handled by background workers, so users never wait for them. Data is stored in a PostgreSQL database and in private encrypted storage. This keeps the system simple to run, responsive, and easy to expand later.Some components below are implemented today and others are design targets; see Section 11 for the status of each.

docs.title: 7. Identity and Access Management
docs.text: Controls in this section are the target design unless marked Implemented or Planned in Section 11.

docs.title: 7.1 Authentication
docs.text:
• Email and password with hashed passwords and a breached-password check.
  • Short-lived, single-use email OTP with attempt limits.
  • Funders and admins also Planned to use TOTP or passkeys.
  • Short-lived access tokens with rotating refresh tokens, stored in httpOnly, Secure, SameSite cookies. A reused refresh token revokes the whole token family, and a server-side store allows logout and account suspension. Current state: the backend defines a refresh cookie (knode_refresh), but the frontend currently keeps tokens in sessionStorage, does not call /auth/refresh, and does not implement logout. Cookie-based rotation is Planned for the frontend.
  • Per-account and per-IP throttling with progressive lockout.

docs.title: 7.2 Authorization
docs.text:
• Role-based access control for NGO member, NGO admin, Funder member, Funder admin and KNode admin.
  • Every request checks ownership of the object, not just the role.
  • Requests without a resolved tenant are rejected.

docs.title: 7.3 Organization verification
docs.text:
1. The EIN is checked against IRS exempt organization data and must be listed and not revoked.
  2. The applicant's email domain must match the organization's website.
  3. An OTP sent to a verified-domain email confirms control of the domain.
  4. Unverified or mismatched applications are held for admin review.

Verification status is re-checked on a schedule to detect later IRS revocations.

docs.title: 8. Data Protection and Tenant Isolation
docs.text:
Controls in this section are the target design unless marked Implemented or Planned in Section 11.

  • Encryption: data is encrypted at rest and in transit, and sensitive fields are encrypted again at application level.
  • Row-Level Security (RLS): PostgreSQL Row-Level Security is the planned mechanism for tenant isolation. Today, isolation relies on application-level scope checks, which are still being verified route by route.
  • Tenant context: the API sets the tenant for every request inside the database transaction. Application database roles cannot bypass RLS, and automated tests attempt cross-tenant access on every tenant-private table.
  • Shared data: published profile fields, verified capabilities and published opportunities are readable by authenticated users according to a visibility flag, so funders can discover organizations.
  • Documents: uploads are stored privately with SSE-KMS encryption and served only through short-lived pre-signed URLs.
  • Secrets and keys: held in the secrets manager and KMS with least-privilege access and key rotation.
  • Backups: encrypted, daily, kept for 30 days in a separate region, with quarterly restore tests.

docs.title: 9. Upload, Ingestion and AI Gateway Controls
docs.text:
Controls in this section are the target design unless marked Implemented or Planned in Section 11.

  • Uploads: file type allowlist, size and page limits, content-type check, malware scan and sandboxed parsing.
  • Ingestion: allow-listed targets only, protection against server-side request forgery, isolated workers, and scraped content treated as untrusted.
  • AI Service Gateway: personal data is redacted before any text leaves the platform, source text is passed as untrusted data, and results are validated against the source before being saved. Records from documents flagged as suspected injections are held for review rather than published automatically. Per-tenant quotas limit misuse.

docs.title: 10. Audit and Logging
docs.text:
Controls in this section are the target design unless marked Implemented or Planned in Section 11.

  • Authentication, OTP, access and privileged-action events are logged, with critical data changes.
  • Logs are append-only and kept for 12 months.
  • Logs never contain passwords, OTPs, keys or document content.

This page documents the KNode web frontend as implemented in the alya-frontend-develop repository. It describes the code that exists, not the product plan. Where the MVP document or the OpenAPI spec disagrees with the code, the discrepancy is stated.

Implementation status labels used throughout:

Label Meaning Integrated UI calls a backend endpoint that exists in the bundled OpenAPI spec Integrated, path mismatch UI calls an endpoint whose path differs from the bundled spec Static data UI works from data embedded in the frontend Placeholder Control or page exists but is disabled, hard-coded or absent Absent No code found

docs.title: 1. Frontend Overview
docs.text:
The frontend is a Next.js web dashboard with two role-specific areas that share one application shell:

  • NGO area (/ngo/*): dashboard, opportunity search and detail, match assessments with partner suggestions, collectives and the consortium workspace, trend analysis, organisation profile and evidence documents.
  • Funder area (/funder/*): dashboard, grant (opportunity) management with AI-assisted extraction from an uploaded file, organisation discovery with evidence view, coalition (collective) review.

It has no server-side logic of its own. Every page is a client component (or a thin server wrapper around one) that calls the KNode REST API directly from the browser. There is no Next.js route handler, server action, or middleware in the repository.

Roles. The backend returns ORGANISATION or FUNDER for the current user (lib/api.ts Role). After login the frontend routes ORGANISATION to /ngo/dashboard and FUNDER to /funder/dashboard (components/auth/otp-form.tsx).

docs.title: 3.1 Shape of the application
docs.text:
The code is organised in four layers. The boundaries are conventional, not enforced by tooling.

flowchart TD
    subgraph Pages["app/ (routes, layouts)"]
        A[Auth pages]
        N["/ngo/* pages"]
        F["/funder/* pages"]
    end
    subgraph Feat["components/features, components/layout, components/auth"]
        C1[Feature components]
        C2["AppShell, Sidebar, Topbar"]
    end

docs.title: 3.2 Entry point and initialisation
docs.text:
• app/layout.tsx is the only root layout. It loads the Outfit font, sets metadata (title: "KNode"), and renders <html lang="en"> with children. It does not mount any provider.
  • app/page.tsx redirects / to /auth/signup.

docs.title: 3.3 Separation of concerns
docs.text:
• Presentation: components/ui/* (generic) and components/features/* (domain-specific cards, panels, lists).
  • Data access: lib/*.ts. Pages call these functions directly; there is no hooks layer for most data. Custom hooks exist only for opportunities (usePagedOpportunities, useAllGrants) and media queries (hooks/UseMediaQuery.ts).
  • Business logic: mixed. Grant form logic is well separated (lib/grantForm.ts, lib/grantFormSchema.ts, lib/grantExtract.ts). Other pages (for example app/ngo/dashboard/page.tsx, app/funder/organisations/page.tsx) combine fetching, derivation and rendering in one file, at 560–720 lines each.

docs.title: 5. Routing and Navigation
docs.text:
Routing uses the Next.js App Router file convention. There is no middleware/proxy file, no not-found.tsx, no error.tsx and no loading.tsx anywhere in app/.

Navigation. lib/nav.ts defines navByRole; Sidebar renders the list for the user's role and marks the active item via pathname.startsWith(href + "/"). Topbar builds a one-level breadcrumb from the path.

Guards. Protection is client-side only:

  • /ngo/*: app/ngo/layout.tsx redirects to /auth/login when fetchCurrentUser() returns null or throws. It does not check that the user's role is ORGANISATION.
  • /funder/*: no guard. The funder layout renders for anyone. Individual funder API calls will return errors for unauthenticated users; the funder dashboard loader additionally throws if role !== "FUNDER" (lib/funder-frontend.ts).
  • /auth/*: no redirect for already-signed-in users.

Invalid routes. Handled by Next.js defaults.

Frontend routing is not authorisation

These checks decide what the interface shows. They do not protect data. The backend must authorise each request by token and role. Given that the funder area has no frontend guard at all, backend enforcement is the only barrier there.

docs.title: 6.1 Flow
docs.text:
Authentication is a two-step, OTP-based flow implemented against /api/v1/auth/*.

sequenceDiagram
    participant U as User
    participant FE as Frontend
    participant API as Backend
    U->>FE: /auth/login (email, password)
    FE->>API: POST /api/v1/auth/login
    API-->>FE: { mfa_required, message }
    FE->>FE: sessionStorage: pending email
    FE->>U: /auth/verify-login (6-digit code)
    U->>FE: code
    FE->>API: POST /api/v1/auth/verify-login
    API-->>FE: { access_token, refresh_token? }
    FE->>FE: sessionStorage: token(s)
    FE->>API: GET /api/v1/auth/me (Bearer)
    API-->>FE: user with role
    FE->>U: /ngo/dashboard or /funder/dashboard
  • Registration: app/auth/signup/page.tsx chooses ORGANISATION or FUNDER, validates with lib/validation.ts (zod: email, password ≥ 8 chars with upper, lower and digit, required names; EIN required for organisations), calls authApi.register, stores the email and goes to /auth/verify-email, then back to /auth/login.
  • OTP entry: components/auth/otp-form.tsx is shared. It supports six single-digit inputs, paste, arrow/backspace navigation, auto-submit on the sixth digit, and autoComplete="one-time-code". It redirects to /auth/login if no pending email is stored.
  • Login 403: login/page.tsx stores the pending email on a 403 but does not redirect to /auth/verify-email; the user only sees the error message.

docs.title: 6.2 Session and token handling
docs.text: Aspect Implementation Storage sessionStorage keys knode_access_token, knode_refresh_token, knode_pending_email (authStorage in lib/api.ts) Sending Authorization: Bearer <token> added by authedRequest; authHeaders() for raw fetches. Requests also use credentials: "include" Persistence Survives refresh in the same tab; lost when the tab closes; not shared between tabs Current user fetchCurrentUser() → GET /api/v1/auth/me; returns null on 401 or when no token Expiry handling A 401 yields null, so /ngo/* redirects to login. Elsewhere there is no global handler Refresh The refresh token is stored but never used. /api/v1/auth/refresh exists in the spec; no frontend code calls it Logout Not implemented. The sidebar "Log out" is a plain link to /auth/login. It does not clear either token and does not call /api/v1/auth/logout

docs.title: 6.3 Roles
docs.text: Role-dependent UI is limited to the sidebar items (navByRole) and the post-login redirect. Role knowledge comes from /auth/me. The NGO layout hard-codes role: "ngo"; the funder layout hard-codes a fake user.

docs.title: 6.4 Responsibilities
docs.text: Frontend Backend (must enforce) Collect credentials, validate format, hold the token, route by role, hide irrelevant navigation Credential and OTP verification, token issue/expiry/revocation, per-endpoint role and ownership checks

docs.title: 7.1 Clients
docs.text:
1. authedRequest<T>(path, options) in lib/api.ts: base NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL (trailing slashes trimmed), adds Accept, JSON Content-Type (not for FormData), bearer token, cache: "no-store", credentials: "include"; throws ApiError(message, status). Network failure gives ApiError("Unable to reach the server…", 0). If the base URL is missing it throws a readable error.
  2. post() (private, lib/api.ts): used by authApi for unauthenticated calls. It does not check for a missing base URL or trim slashes.
  3. Raw fetch helpers in lib/opportunities.ts, lib/grantForm.ts, lib/grantExtract.ts and the opportunity pages: base NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL + /opportunities; errors via readError (returns a string, throws plain Error).

extractMessage (in lib/api.ts) understands three error shapes: { error: { message, details[{field,message}] } }, FastAPI { detail } (string or array with msg), and { message }. lib/opportunities.ts readError handles the first two but not { message }.

docs.title: 7.2 Request lifecycle
docs.text: User action → page handler calls a lib/* function → fetch → JSON parsed → on !res.ok an ApiError/Error is thrown → the page catches it, stores a message in local state and renders an alert; on success the response is stored in useState and rendered. There is no shared cache; every navigation refetches.

docs.title: 7.3 Paging, filtering, sorting
docs.text:
• Opportunities: limit/offset, filters q, status, sector, geography, min_grant, max_grant, deadline_after, deadline_before, sort (lib/filters.ts). These match the spec's query parameters.
  • Organisations (funder): page/page_size (9 per page), q, focus_area, country, verified_only.
  • Evidence: page/page_size, up to 50 pages of 100, with a truncated flag shown in the UI.
  • Matches, collectives, workspace items: limit/offset.
  • Debounce: 250 ms in usePagedOpportunities and useAllGrants, with a cancelled-request guard and a manual retry.

docs.title: 8. Feature Implementation
docs.text: Shared behaviour (token handling, error envelope, paging) is in Sections 6–7 and is not repeated.

docs.title: 8.1 Authentication and account management
docs.text: Pages auth/*, components/auth/otp-form.tsx. Integrated for signup, email verification, login and OTP. Absent: forgot password, logout, account settings.

docs.title: 8.2 NGO opportunity search and detail
docs.text:
• List (app/ngo/opportunities/page.tsx): OpportunityFilters, FilterChips, OpportunityCard, Pagination; data via usePagedOpportunities; loading, error-with-retry, and empty states.
  • Detail (app/ngo/opportunities/[id]/page.tsx): fetches the opportunity and its requirements (raw fetch, 404/422 shown as "could not be found"), loads existing assessments via matchingApi.listAssessments, can run a new assessment via createAssessment, then loads partner suggestions. Renders MatchPanel, RequirementStatus, CoalitionPanel, MatchScoreRing.
  • Options are static. useOptions() in lib/options.ts returns the constant optionsData (statuses, sectors, countries, currencies, limits). It never calls the backend; error is always "" and retry does nothing. Static data.

docs.title: 8.3 Matching results and partner suggestions
docs.text: lib/matching.ts normalises responses so absent arrays become [] and absent fields null. The UI components handle states such as UNKNOWN, evidence coverage and disclaimers (covered by __tests__/matchPanel.test.tsx and matchingComponents.test.tsx). Integrated.

docs.title: 8.4 NGO dashboard
docs.text: app/ngo/dashboard/page.tsx sequentially loads user → organisation → opportunityApi.list() → matchingApi.listAssessments() (default 20) → partner suggestions for the first match only. The "coalitions" shown are those suggestions. Loading, error, and empty states ("No matches yet", "No suggestions yet") exist. Integrated.

docs.title: 8.5 Organisation profile
docs.text: app/ngo/organisation_profile/page.tsx: view and edit (PATCH), evidence documents listed from the evidence ledger (ledgerEntryToDocument), upload with client-side checks (20 MB, extension list defined in the page) and server-status mapping. Truncation notice if more than 5,000 evidence entries. Integrated. Note the limits differ from grant upload (10 MB; .pdf .docx .txt).

docs.title: 8.6 Collectives and consortium workspace (NGO)
docs.text:
• List (app/ngo/collectives/page.tsx): all collectives, tabs derived from my_membership_status (all, active, invited), accept/decline via respondToInvite, per-collective opportunity and workspace lookups.
  • Detail (app/ngo/collectives/[id]/page.tsx): getCollective, getCoverage, getOpportunity, getOrCreateWorkspace (GET, then POST on 404), listAllItems. The page composes TaskList, DocumentList, DiscussionThread, MemberList, RequirementsChecklist, DeadlineList, ConsortiumCapabilities and ApplicationDetail behind Tabs; the exact tab-to-component mapping was not traced. Item creation uses createItem.
  • Discussion threads are a frontend convention. lib/threads.ts stores threads as NOTE workspace items whose title is prefixed [t:<id>]. The backend has no thread concept in the spec.
  • Status: partially implemented. No UI to create a collective, add or invite members (inviteMember is unused), edit or delete items, refresh coverage or request a lead suggestion, although the spec has endpoints for all of these. Whether task creation and status change are both supported in the UI was not traced.

docs.title: 8.7 Trend analysis
docs.text: app/ngo/trends/page.tsx: filters (timeframe, sector, region) call trendApi.getDashboardData; Recharts LineChart in ResponsiveContainer; initial-loading, refreshing, and error states. Integrated. The MVP's "grant gap analysis" is absent here.

docs.title: 8.8 Funder dashboard and grants
docs.text:
• Dashboard: fetchCurrentFunderOpportunities checks role === "FUNDER", pages through opportunities, then loads matches and coalition policy per opportunity (policy failure is swallowed with .catch(() => null)). Integrated; the policy endpoint path differs from the spec.
  • Grant list/detail: useAllGrants (/mine), detail page with delete (DELETE).
  • Grant create/edit: GrantFormPage (mode="create" | "edit"), React Hook Form + zod resolver from buildGrantSchema(options), three steps (About, Funding and requirements, Review), per-step validation (STEP_FIELDS), draft autosave in localStorage (knode_grant_draft_v3).
  • AI extraction: GrantUpload → extractGrantDraft uploads a file (.pdf .docx .txt, ≤ 10 MB), 120 s timeout and cancel support, maps statuses 401/403/413/415/422/502/503 to messages, and pre-fills the form (formFromDraft records which fields were filled, skipped or missing).
  • Publish: publishGrant POSTs the opportunity, then each requirement; on failure it DELETEs the partly created opportunity; a created id is kept in storage so a retry updates rather than duplicates (publishRecovery.test.ts). Edit uses saveGrantChanges (diff of create/patch/delete on requirements).

docs.title: 8.9 Funder organisation discovery
docs.text: app/funder/organisations/page.tsx: search, focus area, country, verified-only, optional ?opportunity_id= to show matches for that grant; 9 per page. Detail page loads the organisation, evidence (paged), matches and opportunities and renders ScoreRing and tabs. Integrated.

docs.title: 8.10 Coalitions (funder)
docs.text: List (funder/coalitions/page.tsx) and detail ([id]/page.tsx) use lib/funderCoalitions.ts and components CoalitionHero, MembersTable, StrengthTiles, EvidencePanel, RequirementsChecklist.

docs.title: 9. UI Components and Design System
docs.text:
Tokens (app/globals.css, Tailwind v4 @theme):

Token group Values Navy navy-900 #17212b, 800 #212d39, 700 #2d3b49, 400 #7f8c99, 300 #a9b4bf Brand orange brand-600 #e07414, 500 #f28a2e, 100 #fde7d0, 50 #fef3e6 Neutrals canvas #f6f5f1, surface #ffffff, line #e7e4dd, ink #1a1d21, ink-muted #5f6770 Font --font-sans = Outfit with system fallbacks

The root font size is clamp(16px, 1.1111vw, 24px), so all rem values scale with viewport width.

Patterns.

  • components/ui/* are small presentational components. Button supports primary | dark | outline | danger, sm | md, renders a Link when href is set and a non-interactive aria-disabled span when disabled. field.ts exports the shared fieldClass input style. cn() in lib/utils.ts merges classes.
  • components/features/* are domain components built from the UI set.
  • Mixed styling: pages in app/auth/* use hard-coded hex values and Tailwind's default orange palette instead of tokens; several features use separate .css files (opportunities.css, funder.css, discover.css, orgProfile.css, organisation_profile.css, filters.css) with their own class names (for example fStepLabel).
  • Feedback: inline role="alert" error text; status Badge/Tag; no toast library; no shared modal component in components/ui (the mobile Sidebar drawer is the one dialog pattern found).
  • Icons: lucide-react only. Assets: public/knode-logo.png, login-meeting.jpeg, signup.jpeg, otp-bg.svg.

Reuse guidance: build new screens from components/ui and the tokens (bg-brand-500, text-ink-muted, border-line). Avoid new hard-coded hex values.

docs.title: 10. State Management and Data Flow
docs.text:
State category Mechanism Authentication sessionStorage + per-layout fetchCurrentUser(); no shared store (AuthProvider is unused) Server data Per-page useState filled in useEffect; no cache or deduplication. /auth/me is re-requested by the NGO layout, dashboard, and collectives helpers Forms React Hook Form (grant form); plain useState elsewhere Filters and paging Component state (useState). Filters are not in the URL, except ?opportunity_id= on the funder organisations page Workspace/collective Local state loaded per page UI state useState; useSyncExternalStore for media queries and the pending email Persistence sessionStorage (tokens, pending email); localStorage (grant draft); a publish-recovery key (PUBLISH_KEY)

Representative flow (NGO opportunities). /ngo/opportunities → filter inputs update useState → toParams → usePagedOpportunities waits 250 ms, calls fetchOpportunityPage with limit/offset → response stored as {items,total,loading,error} → OpportunityCard list and Pagination render; a stale response is ignored via the cancelled flag.

The distinction between server state and UI state is not formalised; both live in component state.

docs.title: 11. Forms, Validation, and User Feedback
docs.text:
• Auth forms: noValidate forms, zod-backed validators from lib/validation.ts, field errors with aria-invalid/aria-describedby and role="alert", submit button disabled while loading or fields are empty, label text "Signing in…".
  • Grant form: zod schema built from options (title ≤ 500, description ≤ 5,000, ≥ 1 country, positive amount, deadline required and future unless status is CLOSED, minimum award ≤ total, non-empty requirement text, valid URL if given). Validation runs per step before advancing (STEP_FIELDS); __tests__/grantFormValidation.test.tsx covers it.
  • Server validation feedback: extractMessage/readError surface the first details[].message, prefixed by field: when present.
  • Duplicate submissions: loading guards in the OTP form and login; publish recovery prevents duplicate grants after a partial failure.
  • Empty and initial states: present on the NGO dashboard and opportunity list; coverage varies by page and was not exhaustively checked.
  • Known quirk: otp-form.tsx sets the message "Enter the 6-digit code sent to your email" into the error state at the start of every submit.
  • Success feedback: mostly navigation or inline text; no toasts.

docs.title: 12. Responsive Design and Accessibility
docs.text:
Responsive. Tailwind breakpoints. AppShell uses useMediaQuery("(min-width: 64rem)"): at lg and above the sidebar is static; below it becomes an off-canvas drawer with overlay. Page padding changes at lg. The login page hides its hero image below lg (other auth pages not checked). Other pages were not individually reviewed at tablet/mobile widths, and no visual or responsive tests exist.

Accessibility patterns verified in code:

  • Sidebar drawer: role="dialog", aria-modal, focus trap, Escape to close, focus returned to the menu button, inert on the hidden aside and on the background content.
  • aria-current="page" on the active nav item; <nav aria-label="Main">.
  • Visually hidden labels (sr-only) on login inputs; show/hide password button with aria-pressed.
  • Tabs implement role="tablist"/"tab" with arrow-key navigation.
  • motion-reduce variants on transitions; focus-visible outlines in the brand colour.
  • aria-live/role="status" appears in several feature components.

Not established: colour-contrast results, screen-reader testing, keyboard testing of every page, automated accessibility tests. WCAG conformance is not claimed.

docs.title: 13. Error Handling, Loading States, and Reliability
docs.text:
Case Behaviour Network failure authedRequest → ApiError(…, 0) with a retry-style message; raw fetch paths show "Could not reach the server." API error Message extracted from the envelope; rendered per page 401 fetchCurrentUser returns null → /ngo/* redirects. Elsewhere pages show the server message. No refresh and no global redirect Missing record Opportunity detail: 404/422 → "could not be found"; workspace 404 → create Empty results Explicit text on several lists Loading Text indicators ("Loading workspace…", "Loading dashboard…") or flags; no skeletons Retry Manual retry in usePagedOpportunities and useAllGrants; no automatic retry or backoff Unexpected errors No error boundaries: no error.tsx or global-error.tsx. An uncaught render error will show Next.js's default error UI Timeouts Only the AI extraction call (120 s)

Raw console.error calls are used for several failures (dashboard, trends, layout).

docs.title: 14. Configuration and Environment Variables
docs.text:
Only process.env references are used; no .env.example exists, and .env* is git-ignored. NEXT_PUBLIC_* values are inlined into the browser bundle at build time.

Variable Purpose Required? Example Placeholder NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL Base URL for authedRequest and authApi (paths already start with /api/v1/..., /collectives, /workspaces) Yes: all authenticated calls https://<api-host> NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL Prefix for OPPORTUNITIES_URL (${NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL}/opportunities) used by opportunity lists, grant CRUD and extraction Yes for opportunities and grants https://<api-host>/api/v1

docs.title: 15. Local Development Setup
docs.text:
1. Prerequisites: Node.js and npm (no engines field or .nvmrc; use a version supported by Next.js 16, unverified), and a running backend that implements the spec in docs/openapi.json.
  2. Get the code and cd alya-frontend-develop.
  3. Install: npm install (a prepare script runs husky, installing the git hook).
  4. Configure: create .env.local with the two variables above.
  5. Run: npm run dev (Next.js default port 3000).
  6. Lint: npm run lint. Format check: npm run format:check.
  7. Type check: there is no script. next build type-checks; npx tsc --noEmit also works with the existing tsconfig.json (not a project script).
  8. Test: npm run test (vitest run, jsdom, setup in vitest.setup.ts).
  9. Build: npm run build, then npm start.

docs.title: 16. Testing and Quality Assurance
docs.text: Area Files Grant extraction logic grantExtract.test.ts, grantUpload.test.tsx Grant form grantFormValidation.test.tsx, publishRecovery.test.ts, editRequirements503.test.tsx Matching UI matchPanel.test.tsx, matchingComponents.test.tsx Opportunity views ngoGrantCard.test.tsx, ngoRequirements503.test.tsx API contract openapiContract.test.ts (spec snapshot only)

docs.title: 17. Build, Deployment, and Production Behaviour
docs.text:
• Build: next build; output is a Next.js server/static build (npm start runs next start).
  • Execution model: the root layout and funder layout are server components; everything else is client-rendered and fetches from the browser.
  • Hosting: Hosted on vercel
  • CI: the only workflow (.github/workflows/pr-ready-check.yml) runs on a self-hosted runner labelled classroom-ci and only checks that the PR template's "Ready for Review" boxes are ticked. It does not run build, lint or tests, although README.md says CI checks "build, lint, tests".
  • Caching and performance: no-store on API calls; no service worker; no explicit performance configuration beyond Next.js defaults.

docs.title: 18. Security Considerations
docs.text:
Verified measures

  • No hard-coded secrets seen in the files reviewed (not a full secret scan); .env* is git-ignored.
  • No dangerouslySetInnerHTML or innerHTML in app, components or lib; user content is rendered through React.
  • Path segments in API URLs use encodeURIComponent in most client code.
  • Input validation on auth and grant forms; upload type/size checks before sending.
  • Token in sessionStorage rather than localStorage, so it does not persist after the tab closes.
