docs.title: About this glossary
docs.text:
This glossary defines the terms used across the KNode technical documentation, grouped by system area. It also contains an abbreviation index.

Sources. Terms come from the Architecture, Backend (index, Database, API Reference, Authentication and Security, Matching Engine, Testing), AI Service, Frontend Web and Integrations pages of the alya-technical-documentation repository (main branch). The Overview page was an empty stub when these sources were read. No source code, ERD, PRD, MVP document, OpenAPI file or Figma file was available, so project-specific claims are checked against the documentation, not against code.

Status labels in the "Context in KNode" column. The documentation mixes target design with inspected code, so entries that describe KNode-specific behaviour say which it is:

Label Meaning Implemented The Backend, AI Service, Frontend or Integrations pages describe it as present in inspected code. Design only Only the Architecture page describes it; the Backend or Frontend pages do not confirm it. Not found A code-based page states it was looked for and not found. Do not describe it as built. Unverified The documentation itself says the behaviour needs checking.

Entries without a label define a general concept and note how KNode uses it.

docs.title: Master glossary
docs.text: Entries are alphabetical within each category. Where a concept has both a database table entry (section D2) and a domain entry, the table entry describes the stored record and the domain entry describes the concept.

docs.title: A. General software engineering
docs.text: Term Definition Context in KNode API (Application Programming Interface) A defined interface through which one piece of software requests data or actions from another. Implemented. The Next.js frontend calls the FastAPI backend's JSON endpoints under the /api/v1 prefix and a few unversioned paths. See also Endpoint, OpenAPI. Build The step that turns source code into something runnable, such as compiling TypeScript or bundling a web app. Implemented. Frontend: npm run build, then npm start. Backend: dependencies are installed with uv; there is no compile step. Client-server architecture A design where a client (here a browser) sends requests to a server that holds the data and rules. Implemented. The browser frontend talks only to the KNode backend; third-party services sit behind the backend, never behind the browser. Component A self-contained, reusable piece of a system. In the frontend it means a React UI element; in the architecture it means a major function such as Matching Engine or Referrals. Implemented. The Architecture page lists 14 system components. The Frontend page groups UI components into ui, features, layout and auth. Configuration Settings that change how an application behaves without changing its code. Implemented. Backend settings load from .env via pydantic-settings; frontend settings are NEXT_PUBLIC_* variables. See Environment variable. Correlation ID A unique identifier attached to a request so every log line and error response for that request can be linked. Implemented. Backend middleware installs it; the documentation says it is not yet returned consistently. Dependency An external library or package that code needs in order to run. Also, in FastAPI, a function that supplies a value to a route (see Dependency injection). Implemented. Python dependencies are declared in pyproject.toml and locked in uv.lock; npm packages in package.json. The Backend page flags the httpx2 entry for verification. Environment A separate running copy of the system with its own database, keys and settings. Implemented as the ENV setting (dev, test, staging, prod), which changes email and cookie behaviour. The Architecture page describes separate dev, staging and production stacks (Design only). Integration A connection between KNode and a third-party service or data source. Implemented. Documented integrations: Google Gemini, SMTP email, PostgreSQL, USAspending, Grants.gov, IRS data, ProPublica, Candid, GlobalGiving. See the Integrations page. Layered architecture Organising code into layers that each have one job and call only the layer beneath. Implemented. Backend: routers, then Pydantic schemas, services, repositories, SQLAlchemy models, with core modules for config, security and errors. Frontend: pages, feature components, UI components, then lib. The frontend page notes its boundaries are convention, not enforced. Middleware Code that runs on every request before or after the route handler. Implemented. Correlation-ID middleware and CORS are registered in main.py. The frontend has no Next.js middleware. Module A file or folder of related code with a clear responsibility. Also used in the Architecture page for a product capability. Implemented. For example services/matching_engine/ is a backend module. Repository (data-access layer) A class or module that wraps database queries so business code does not write them directly. Implemented. The backend repositories/ folder, for example matching_repository.py. Not the same as a source-control repository. Repository (source control) A version-controlled project folder, such as a Git repository. The documentation refers to the alya-technical-documentation, alya-frontend-develop and backend repositories. Runtime The environment in which code executes, or the period while it executes. Backend: Python 3.11 or newer with Uvicorn. Frontend: Node.js with Next.js (version not pinned by an engines field). Service (backend business-logic layer) A module that implements a business workflow, applying rules and calling repositories and external providers. Implemented. services/ holds auth_service, matching_service, email_service and others. Routers delegate to services. Service (external) A third-party system KNode calls, such as Gemini or an SMTP server. See Integration. uv A Python package and environment manager. Implemented. README commands: uv venv, uv pip install -r pyproject.toml --group dev, uv run ...

docs.title: B. Frontend and user interface
docs.text: Term Definition Context in KNode Absent / Integrated / Integrated, path mismatch / Placeholder / Static data The five implementation-status labels used on the Frontend page. Integrated: the UI calls a backend endpoint that exists in the bundled OpenAPI snapshot. Integrated, path mismatch: it calls a path that differs from the snapshot. Static data: it uses data embedded in the frontend. Placeholder: a control or page exists but is disabled or hard-coded. Absent: no code found. Project-specific labels. Use them only for the frontend; the status labels in this glossary (Implemented, Design only, and so on) are a different scheme. ApiError / authedRequest authedRequest() is the frontend's main HTTP helper: it adds the bearer token, JSON headers and cache: "no-store", then throws ApiError(message, status) on failure. Implemented in lib/api.ts. Some opportunity and grant calls bypass it with raw fetch and the NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL base. App Router The Next.js routing system in which folders under app/ become URL routes and layout.tsx files wrap them. Implemented. Routes include /auth/*, /ngo/* and /funder/*. AppShell The shared frame (sidebar, top bar, page header) used by the NGO and funder areas. Implemented in components/layout/. Below 64rem the sidebar becomes an off-canvas drawer. Client-side rendering (CSR) Building the page in the browser using JavaScript, with data fetched from the browser. Implemented. Almost every page is a client component that calls the API directly. Debounce Waiting a short time after the last input before acting, to avoid a request per keystroke. Implemented: 250 ms in usePagedOpportunities and useAllGrants. Design tokens Named values for colours, fonts and spacing that keep styling consistent. Implemented as Tailwind @theme tokens in app/globals.css: navy-, brand-, canvas, surface, line, ink. Auth pages still use hard-coded hex values. Draft autosave Saving an unfinished form so it survives a refresh. Implemented for the grant form in localStorage under knode_grant_draft_v3. The draft persists after logout. Empty state What a screen shows when a list has no items. Implemented on several lists ("No matches yet", "No suggestions yet"). Coverage across pages was not exhaustively checked. Error boundary A framework mechanism that catches rendering errors and shows a fallback screen. In Next.js: error.tsx and global-error.tsx. Not found. The Frontend page states none exist, so an uncaught render error shows the Next.js default. Funder area / NGO area The two role-specific parts of the frontend: /funder/* and /ngo/*. Both share one application shell. Implemented. The NGO area serves ORGANISATION users; the funder area serves FUNDER users. Hook A React function (useState, useEffect, or a custom use... function) that adds state or behaviour to a component. Implemented. Custom hooks: usePagedOpportunities, useAllGrants, useMediaQuery. Layout A Next.js file that wraps all pages beneath it. app/layout.tsx sets the font and metadata. app/ngo/layout.tsx redirects to login when no user resolves. The funder layout has no guard. Loading state What the UI shows while data is being fetched. Implemented as text ("Loading dashboard…") or flags. No skeletons and no loading.tsx. Next.js A React framework providing routing, layouts, rendering modes and builds. Implemented. Declared version 16.4.1 using the App Router. NEXT_PUBLIC_ variable A Next.js environment variable that is copied into the browser bundle at build time and is therefore public. NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL (authenticated calls) and NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL (opportunities). Never put secrets in them. Pagination (limit / offset) Returning a long list in pages. limit is the page size; offset is how many items to skip. Some endpoints use page and page_size instead. Implemented. Opportunities, matches, collectives and workspace items use limit/offset; funder organisation search and evidence use page/page_size. Publish recovery Logic that prevents duplicate records when a multi-request save fails part-way. Implemented in publishGrant: it creates the opportunity, then each requirement; on failure it deletes the partial opportunity, and a stored id lets a retry update instead of duplicating. React A JavaScript library for building user interfaces from components. Implemented. Declared version 19.3.0. React Hook Form A library for managing form state and validation. Implemented for the grant form only; other forms use plain useState. Recharts A charting library for React. Implemented: the trend LineChart on /ngo/trends. Responsive design Layouts that adapt to screen width. Implemented with Tailwind breakpoints. No visual or responsive tests exist. Route guard Client-side code that redirects users who should not see a page. Implemented only for /ngo/*, and it checks that a user exists, not their role. It controls what the interface shows; it does not protect data. Routing Mapping a URL to a page. See App Router. sessionStorage / localStorage Browser storage. sessionStorage is cleared when the tab closes; localStorage persists until removed. Tokens and the pending email are in sessionStorage (knode_access_token, knode_refresh_token, knode_pending_email); the grant draft is in localStorage. State management How an application stores and shares data that changes. Implemented with React hooks and component state. No Redux, Zustand, SWR or React Query. An AuthProvider context exists but is unused. Tailwind CSS A utility-first CSS framework. Implemented, version 4. Several features also use separate plain .css files. TypeScript JavaScript with static types. Implemented, strict: true, path alias @/*. Zod A TypeScript schema-validation library. Implemented for auth fields (lib/validation.ts) and the grant form schema.

docs.title: C. Backend and API development
docs.text: Term Definition Context in KNode API contract The agreed shape of requests, responses, status codes and errors between client and server. The live contract is the backend's /openapi.json. The frontend keeps a snapshot at docs/openapi.json; openapiContract.test.ts checks that snapshot, not the live backend. The Backend page says the endpoint inventory is a map, not the contract. Business logic The rules that decide what the system does, as opposed to plumbing such as HTTP or storage. Implemented in backend services/ and the pure functions in services/matching_engine/. The Backend page says to keep it out of routers. CORS (Cross-Origin Resource Sharing) A browser rule that blocks a page from calling a different origin unless that server explicitly allows it. Implemented. The backend allows only origins in CORS_ALLOW_ORIGINS (default http://localhost:3000). Production values must be set explicitly. CRUD Create, Read, Update, Delete: the four basic data operations. Used for opportunities, requirements, organisations, funders, collectives and workspace items. Not every entity exposes all four. Dependency injection A pattern where a function declares what it needs and the framework supplies it. Implemented through FastAPI Depends. get_db supplies the database session; get_current_user, require_role and the scope helpers supply the caller. Endpoint / route A URL path plus HTTP method that the server handles, such as POST /api/v1/matches. A route is the code definition; an endpoint is the resulting URL. Implemented. The API Reference inventories them by feature. Exception handler Code that converts a raised error into a client-safe HTTP response. Implemented, but registered in two places, core/errors.py and core/error_handlers.py. FastAPI A Python web framework that builds JSON APIs from typed functions and generates OpenAPI documentation. Implemented. App title KNode, version 0.1.0, served by Uvicorn. HTTP method The verb of a request: GET (read), POST (create or act), PATCH (partial update), DELETE. Used throughout. Some paths accept several methods (for example GET/POST /collectives). JSON (JavaScript Object Notation) A text format for structured data. All API bodies, Gemini responses and several database columns. OpenAPI A standard machine-readable description of an HTTP API. FastAPI generates it at /openapi.json, with an interactive page at /docs. Postman can import it. Path / query parameter A value in the URL path (/matches/{match_id}) or after the ? (?limit=20). limit is 1 to 100 (default 20) and offset at least 0 on GET /api/v1/matches. Pydantic model / schema A Python class that declares fields and types, validates data against them, and can export a JSON schema. Implemented. In schemas/ for requests and responses (MatchCreateRequest, MatchResponse). Also used to force Gemini output into a shape (ExtractedProfile, ExtractedEvidence). REST API An HTTP API organised around resources and standard methods. KNode describes itself as exposing JSON HTTP endpoints. Route prefixes are not fully uniform. Request schema / response schema The Pydantic models that define what a client may send and what the server returns. response_model shapes outputs, so internal fields are not leaked. Router A FastAPI object that groups related routes under one prefix. Implemented: routers/auth.py, matching.py, collectives.py and so on. Status code A three-digit HTTP result. 201 created; 401 bad token; 403 forbidden; 404 not found (sometimes used deliberately instead of 403); 409 conflict; 422 validation; 423 account locked; 429 too many OTP attempts; 502 extraction failed; 503 extraction unavailable; 500 unhandled. Uvicorn An ASGI server that runs FastAPI apps. uv run --no-sync uvicorn main:app --reload for local runs. Versioned route A route under /api/v1. Most routes are versioned; collectives, referrals, workspaces and evidence are documented as unversioned.

docs.title: D1. General database concepts
docs.text: Term Definition Context in KNode Alembic A migration tool for SQLAlchemy that keeps a versioned history of schema changes. Implemented. Files in alembic/versions/; commands alembic heads, alembic current, alembic upgrade head. The latest noted revision, b4f783d2d110, merges two branches; verify current heads. Cascade / SET NULL Rules for what happens to child rows when a parent row is deleted: CASCADE deletes them; SET NULL clears the reference. opportunity_requirements cascade when their opportunity is deleted. workspace_items assignee and author references may use SET NULL. Check constraint A database rule that every row must satisfy a condition. referrals requires exactly one target: an organisation or a collective. Constraint A rule enforced by the database: not null, unique, foreign key, check. Provides an integrity boundary beyond Pydantic and service checks. Entity / table / model An entity is a thing the system stores. A table holds its rows; a SQLAlchemy model is the Python class mapped to the table. The documentation uses the table name (organisations) and the model name (Organisation) interchangeably. Enum (database) A column limited to a fixed set of values. Many enums use native_enum=False, stored as text rather than a PostgreSQL enum type. Examples: UserRole, UserStatus, opportunity status, coalition_policy. Foreign key A column that references another table's primary key, so the database can reject orphaned references. Used throughout, for example opportunity_requirements.opportunity_id. ai_files is the exception (see Polymorphic association). GUID / UUID A 128-bit identifier that is practically unique without central coordination. Primary keys such as user_id and match_id. A custom GUID type in models/types.py works on both PostgreSQL and SQLite; verify on both. Index A structure that speeds up lookups on a column. Index definitions are not described in the documentation; the migration checklist says to review them. JSON vs JSONB JSON stores text; PostgreSQL JSONB stores a binary, indexable form. KNode uses SQLAlchemy generic JSON, not JSONB, for focus_areas, capabilities, structured_value, score_breakdown, requirement_assessments and report content. Migration A versioned script that changes the database schema. See Alembic. Run as a controlled release step; create_all() in tests is not a substitute. Numeric(19,4) An exact decimal with up to 19 digits and 4 after the point, used for money to avoid floating-point error. Grant minimums and maximums, revenue. Currency is a separate CHAR(3) column. ORM (Object-Relational Mapping) A technique that maps Python classes to database tables so queries are written in Python. Implemented with SQLAlchemy 2.x. pgvector A PostgreSQL extension for storing embeddings and searching by vector similarity. Design only. The Architecture page lists it; the Backend page says no pgvector or embedding code was found in the matching path. Polymorphic association One table referencing several kinds of parent through a type column plus an id column, without a normal foreign key. ai_files.entity_type + entity_id. The database cannot enforce that the target exists. PostgreSQL An open-source relational database. Implemented. The system of record, configured with DATABASE_URL. Primary key The column that uniquely identifies a row. A UUID per table, such as organisation_id. Referential integrity The guarantee that references between rows stay valid. Enforced by foreign keys; SQLite tests enable foreign keys explicitly. Relationship A link between two tables. One-to-many: one parent row, many child rows (an opportunity has many requirements). Many-to-many: rows on both sides can link to many on the other, through a join table. collective_members is the membership link between collectives and members. The documentation does not name the member column; the coverage code uses Organisation, so organisations are the members (verify). Schema (database) vs schema (Pydantic) A database schema is the set of tables and columns. A Pydantic schema is an API request or response shape. Context decides which is meant. The Backend page treats the live database schema and the models as potentially different. Session (SQLAlchemy) A unit of work holding database connections and pending changes. SessionLocal has autocommit=False and autoflush=False; get_db() closes it in a finally block. Closing does not commit. SQLAlchemy The Python ORM and SQL toolkit. Implemented, version 2.x. SQLite A file or in-memory database. Implemented for tests only, with StaticPool. It does not prove PostgreSQL behaviour. Timestamp A date-time value. Models declare timezone-aware DateTime columns. deadline_at is explicitly timezone-aware. Transaction A group of database changes that all succeed or all roll back. Boundaries differ by service; repositories/transaction.py is the place to inspect. Atomicity of matching writes is unverified. Unique constraint A rule that a value, or combination, cannot repeat. users.email, organisations.ein, and the composite (source_system, external_id) on opportunities and awards.

docs.title: D2. KNode tables, fields and enumerations
docs.text: Term Definition Context in KNode ai_files Records of files handled by the AI and document pipeline, linked to an organisation, funder or opportunity through a polymorphic association. Implemented. Distinct from sources, which records evidence provenance. How the two relate is not fully documented. algorithm_version A label recording which scoring logic produced a match run. Stored on match_runs. The AI Service page names the scoring weights set match-score-v1; whether that string is the stored value is unverified. audit_events Rows recording who did what, to which target, when. Model and service Implemented; complete audit coverage is Unverified. ORM attribute event_metadata maps to the column metadata. coalition_policy A field on a funding opportunity stating the funder's stance on applicants forming coalitions. Enum, default UNSPECIFIED. Implemented. Only UNSPECIFIED is documented; the other values are not listed. Read via GET /api/v1/matches/opportunities/{id}/coalition-policy. collective_members One row per member of a collective, with participation and response state. Implemented. Membership uniqueness and response timestamps are constrained. Status values are not enumerated. collectives A group of organisations assembled around a funding opportunity. Implemented. See Collective in section H. confidence_score A number (Numeric(5,2)) on an extracted claim indicating how sure the extraction was. Implemented in the schema. How it is produced and whether it is used downstream is not documented; the scoring formula does not reference it. dedupe_key An optional key inside a requirement's structured value, used to merge duplicate requirements before scoring. Implemented in the scoring module. The first requirement with the key is kept; conflicts produce warnings. ein Employer Identification Number: a US tax identifier, nine characters. Stored on organisations (unique, nullable). Required at sign-up for organisations. Used by verification (Design only) against IRS data. extracted_claims A single fact about an organisation, extracted from a source, with evidence text, confidence and review status. Implemented. See Extracted claim in section F. funders Organisations that offer funding. Implemented. Fields: name, funder_type, focus areas, geographic focus, typical grant range, currency. funding_awards Historical records of grants already awarded. Implemented. Source for the Funding Trends analysis. Unique on (source_system, external_id) and linked to a source. Not the same as a funding opportunity. funding_opportunities An open or upcoming call for applications from a funder. Implemented. Fields include title, sector, grant range, currency, deadline_at, status (OPEN, CLOSED, UPCOMING, UNKNOWN), eligible geographies and organisation types. is_mandatory A boolean on a requirement saying whether it is compulsory. Default true. Whether scoring treats mandatory and optional requirements differently is not documented. last_verified_at Timestamp of the last verification of an organisation or funder. Implemented on both tables. The funder organisation search has a verified_only filter, but the documentation does not say which field it reads. match_partners Suggested partner organisations attached to a match. Implemented. Suggestions are computed from stored assessments and always carry participation_confirmed = false. match_runs One execution of a matching workflow: who asked, what type, status, algorithm version, timing, errors. Implemented. Statuses: PENDING, RUNNING, COMPLETED, FAILED. Run types: opportunity matching, partner discovery, collective building. matches The result of assessing one organisation (optionally against one opportunity): score, score breakdown, per-requirement assessments, explanation. Implemented. Score is nullable; a legacy placeholder zero is detected and not shown as a real score. opportunity_requirements One requirement from a funding opportunity, with text, type, mandatory flag, optional structured value and source. Implemented. Types written by extraction: eligibility, geography, thematic_fit, financial_capacity, partnership, evidence. organisation_email_domains The email domains associated with an organisation. Implemented. Supports the planned domain check in verification (Design only). organisations NGOs or other implementing organisations that seek funding. Implemented. Fields: legal and display name, EIN, mission, focus areas, countries, capabilities, registration status, revenue, last_verified_at. published_weight An optional weight the funder publishes for a requirement. When all requirements have positive published weights they replace the default category weights. referrals A record directed at exactly one target, an organisation or a collective, with respond and withdraw actions and a versioned disclaimer (REFERRAL_DISCLAIMER_VERSION). Implemented in schema and routes. A check constraint requires exactly one target. Statuses are not documented. reports Stored report content as JSON. Table exists; a public report router was not found. requirement_assessments A JSON column on matches holding the status, evidence and quote for each requirement. Implemented. Source of the per-requirement view shown in the UI. review_status The state of an extracted claim: PENDING (default), CONFIRMED, DISPUTED. Implemented. Only CONFIRMED claims with non-empty evidence text are used in matching. score_breakdown A JSON column on matches holding the contribution of each scoring category. Implemented. source_system / external_id A code naming where a record came from, plus that source's own id. Values documented: USASPENDING, GRANTS_GOV, CRAWLER, MANUAL. Together they prevent duplicate imports. sources A record of a document or web page that evidence came from: URL or file reference, type, retrieval and publication dates, content, hash. Implemented. See Source document in section I. structured_value A JSON field on a requirement that holds machine-readable detail such as category, published weight and dedupe key. Implemented, optional. users Accounts. Each has a role (ORGANISATION, FUNDER, ADMIN), a status (ACTIVE, INACTIVE, SUSPENDED) and an optional organisation or funder link. Implemented. The password is stored only as an Argon2 hash. workspace_items The things inside a workspace: tasks, documents and notes, with optional author and assignee. Implemented. The frontend also stores discussion threads as NOTE items (see Discussion thread). workspaces A shared work area attached to one collective. Implemented. See Consortium workspace in section H.

docs.title: E. Authentication, authorisation and security
docs.text:
The Architecture page describes a larger security design than the Backend and Frontend pages confirm. Entries marked Design only should not be presented as built.

Term Definition Context in KNode Access token A short-lived credential sent with each request to prove who the caller is. Implemented. A JWT valid 900 seconds (15 minutes) by default (ACCESS_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS), sent as Authorization: Bearer. Argon2 A deliberately slow, memory-hungry password-hashing algorithm. Implemented through PasswordHasher in core/security.py. Audit log / audit event An append-only record of security-relevant actions. Model and service Implemented; coverage Unverified. The Architecture page describes 12-month append-only retention (Design only). Authentication vs authorisation Authentication proves who you are (password plus one-time code). Authorisation decides what that identity may do (role and ownership checks). Authentication: /api/v1/auth/*. Authorisation: require_role, require_organisation_scope, require_funder_scope. A valid token alone never implies access to a given record. Bearer token A token that grants access to whoever presents it. Sent in the Authorization header by authedRequest. The frontend also sends credentials: "include". Cookie attributes (HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite) Flags that keep a cookie away from page scripts, restrict it to HTTPS, and limit cross-site sending. Backend settings: cookie knode_refresh, REFRESH_COOKIE_SECURE=true, SameSite=lax. The frontend stores the refresh token in sessionStorage instead. Cross-tenant access One organisation or funder reading or changing another's private data. The central authorisation risk. The Backend page lists cross-organisation and cross-funder tests as required checks. See Tenant isolation. Data privacy / redaction Removing personal or sensitive data before it is stored, logged or sent elsewhere. Implemented for Gemini evidence prompts: email-like strings become [email removed], and database ids and organisation names are not sent. Logs hold error types, not document text. Environment variable A named value supplied by the environment rather than written in code. Implemented. Examples: DATABASE_URL, JWT_SECRET, GEMINI_API_KEY. Input validation Checking that incoming data has the expected type, length and format. Pydantic on the backend; zod on the frontend; file type, size and signature checks on uploads. JWT (JSON Web Token) A signed token carrying claims. Implemented with PyJWT. Claims: sub (user), type (access, refresh, email verification, password reset), iat, exp, jti. Signed with JWT_SECRET using HS256 by default. jti / revocation jti is a random id for one token, so a specific token can be revoked. Implemented. Dependencies check the jti and a per-user revoked-after-issued-at time. Revocation state is process-local unless stored shared. KMS (Key Management Service) A managed service that holds encryption keys. Design only. Architecture: SSE-KMS for uploads and key rotation. Current uploads go to UPLOAD_DIR. Least privilege Giving each user or component only the access it needs. Stated as a principle for secrets and keys (Design only). Backend roles are broad (organisation, funder, admin). Lockout Temporarily blocking an account after repeated failed logins. Implemented: LOGIN_MAX_ATTEMPTS=5, LOGIN_LOCKOUT_SECONDS=900; returns 423. OTP (one-time password) A short numeric code valid once, delivered by email. Implemented. Six digits, 600 seconds, 5 attempts. Stored hashed (SHA-256, constant-time compare). Used for sign-up verification and for every login (a second step). Password hashing Storing a one-way transform of the password, never the password. Implemented with Argon2. Minimum length setting is 12. Permission / role A role is a named bundle of permissions. Database roles: ORGANISATION, FUNDER, ADMIN. The Architecture page lists five. Prompt injection Text inside a document that tries to give the AI new instructions. Implemented mitigations: untrusted-text markers, marker stripping, no database ids in prompts, quote verification. See Untrusted input. Protected route An endpoint that requires a valid token. Implemented through the get_current_user dependency. The frontend's /ngo/* guard is cosmetic. RBAC (Role-Based Access Control) Granting access according to a user's role. Implemented by role dependencies, which the Backend page says do not replace object-level checks. Refresh token A longer-lived credential used to obtain new access tokens. Backend default 43,200 seconds (12 hours). The frontend stores but never calls the refresh endpoint. Resource scope A check that the caller may access this particular organisation or funder. require_organisation_scope, require_funder_scope. require_self_or_admin does not currently compare ids, so it is not a reliable ownership check. Row-Level Security (RLS) A PostgreSQL feature that filters rows by policy for each database user. Design only. Not mentioned in the Backend page. Secret A value that grants access if disclosed: keys, passwords, tokens. JWT_SECRET (at least 32 characters), GEMINI_API_KEY, SMTP_PASSWORD. Never commit them or show real values in documentation. Tenant isolation Ensuring each customer organisation's private data is invisible to others. Intended to be enforced by application role and scope checks, whose route-by-route verification is still outstanding. Some routes return 404 to avoid revealing that another tenant's record exists. Database-level RLS is Design only. TOTP / passkey Time-based one-time passwords from an authenticator app; passkeys are device-bound credentials replacing passwords. Design only. Planned for funders and admins. Untrusted input Any text from uploads, websites or model output, treated as data and never as instructions or permissions. Implemented principle across AI paths. Model output cannot grant access or write arbitrary database values. User session The period during which a user is signed in. The frontend keeps it as tokens in sessionStorage. Logout is not implemented in the frontend (the sidebar link neither clears tokens nor calls the logout endpoint). WAF / DDoS protection A web application firewall filters malicious requests; DDoS protection absorbs floods of traffic. Design only. Architecture lists Cloudflare and an API gateway. Not mentioned in code-based pages.

docs.title: F. AI, evidence and matching
docs.text:
KNode's documented design is that AI reads and checks evidence while fixed rules compute eligibility, score and explanation. The AI never computes the score. No machine-learning training, embeddings or vector search is documented in the matching path.

Term Definition Context in KNode AI (artificial intelligence) / LLM (large language model) Software that performs tasks needing language understanding; an LLM is a model trained on text to generate and interpret language. Implemented. Google Gemini is the only model provider documented. Used for three jobs: extracting organisation facts, extracting funding calls, and checking evidence against a requirement. Assessment provider The component that decides a requirement's status from retrieved evidence. Implemented behind an AssessmentProvider interface so it can be mocked; provider_factory.py returns the Gemini provider or disables it. Off by default (AI_ASSESSMENT_ENABLED=false). Capability gap A requirement the lead organisation does not clearly meet. Implemented as a rule: a lead requirement with status UNKNOWN, NOT_CHECKED, ERROR, NOT_MET or PARTIALLY_MET is treated as a gap. A gap is not a proven weakness, because missing evidence is counted too. Complementary organisation An organisation with MET or PARTIALLY_MET evidence for a requirement the lead has as a gap. Implemented as deterministic comparison of stored assessments, labelled "may complement". It does not use semantic search and does not confirm the partner is willing or available. Data extraction / evidence extraction Turning unstructured text or files into structured fields with a source. Implemented. Website text, uploaded PDF, DOCX, PNG and TXT go to Gemini and return schema-validated JSON. Document facts become PENDING claims. Eligibility (condition and overall status) Whether the organisation meets hard conditions of an opportunity. Each condition is SATISFIED, FAILED, UNKNOWN or ERROR; the overall result is ELIGIBLE, INELIGIBLE, NEEDS_VERIFICATION, ERROR or NOT_ASSESSED. Implemented with three conditions only: deadline not passed, geography overlap (no overlap is UNKNOWN, not a failure), organisation type (always UNKNOWN; no logic yet). A satisfied or failed condition with no evidence reference is downgraded to UNKNOWN. Kept separate from the score. Evidence coverage The share of applicable requirement weight that could be assessed. Implemented: 100 x assessed weight / total applicable weight. Score status is COMPLETE, PROVISIONAL or NOT_CALCULABLE. Evidence-backed matching / explainability Every match result can be traced to the quotes and sources behind it, so a person can see why. The project's central principle. Implemented through claim and source ids kept on each assessment and a template explanation built from the score breakdown. The AI does not write the explanation. Extracted claim A single fact about an organisation (for example a country of operation or a capability) with the supporting evidence text, its source, a confidence value and a review status. Implemented (extracted_claims). Claims from uploads start PENDING; a person sets CONFIRMED or DISPUTED. Only CONFIRMED claims with non-empty evidence text reach matching. Website-scraped profile data skips this step. False positive / false negative A false positive is a match or status wrongly reported as good; a false negative is a real fit wrongly missed or marked bad. Not measured. The Backend page lists measuring retrieval quality, false positives and false negatives as outstanding work. The design guards against false negatives by using UNKNOWN for missing evidence. Gemini Google's family of generative AI models. Model name in GEMINI_MODEL; documented default gemini-3.8-flash, which the Backend page asks to confirm. Called with an API key or, as fallback, Vertex AI. Grounding / quote verification Checking that the model's cited quote really appears in the passage it cites. Implemented. The cited passage label must map to a retrieved claim and the quote must appear after whitespace and case normalisation; otherwise the status becomes UNKNOWN. A valid quote does not prove correct interpretation. Human-in-the-loop (human oversight) A person must approve AI output before it takes effect. Implemented at two points: confirming or disputing PENDING claims, and reviewing a draft opportunity before it is saved. Lexical retrieval / information retrieval Finding candidate evidence by matching words rather than meaning. Implemented. Text is tokenised; shared alphanumeric tokens of at least three characters count as overlap; at most five passages go to the provider. May miss differently worded evidence. Match The stored result of assessing an organisation against an opportunity. Implemented (matches). Carries a nullable score, score breakdown, per-requirement assessments, strengths and gaps, missing information, eligibility status and explanation. Match run One execution of a matching workflow that produces matches. Implemented (match_runs): types opportunity matching, partner discovery, collective building; statuses PENDING, RUNNING, COMPLETED, FAILED. Match score A number from 0 to 100 summarising how well assessed requirements are met. Implemented as a deterministic weighted formula, rounded to one decimal (ROUND_HALF_UP). It measures capability alignment, not funding probability or eligibility. Whether showing a number is approved product policy is unconfirmed. Matching engine The backend module that assesses requirements, checks eligibility, scores, finds partners and summarises collective coverage. Implemented in services/matching_engine/. The Architecture page describes it as scoring "using fixed rules". Partner discovery Suggesting organisations that may fill a lead organisation's gaps. Implemented at GET /api/v1/matches/{match_id}/partners. Suggestions always set participation_confirmed to false and include a disclaimer. Passage A piece of confirmed evidence text with its claim, source and organisation ids, sent to the provider. Implemented. Labelled P1, P2 and so on in prompts, and mapped back to ids afterwards. Requirement assessment status The verdict on one requirement: MET, PARTIALLY_MET, NOT_MET, UNKNOWN, NOT_CHECKED (no provider configured), ERROR (provider failure or invalid output). Implemented. NOT_MET requires an explicit contradiction, never just missing evidence. A legacy contract maps SUPPORTED, PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED, UNVERIFIED to MET, PARTIALLY_MET, UNKNOWN. Scoring categories and weights Five groups of requirements with default weights: programme strategic alignment 0.25, programme delivery capability 0.25, experience and track record 0.20, target population and context 0.15, team capacity 0.15. Implemented (set called match-score-v1 in the AI page). Points: MET 4, PARTIALLY_MET 2, NOT_MET 0, maximum 4. Only these three statuses are scored. Funder-published weights replace defaults when complete. Semantic similarity / embedding / vector search Comparing meaning using numeric vectors (embeddings) and finding nearest matches, often with a vector index such as pgvector. Not found in the matching path; the Backend page warns not to describe it as implemented. The Architecture page lists a pgvector store for chunks and embeddings (Design only). Structured output / structured data Data in a fixed machine-readable shape. Structured output means forcing the model to reply in JSON matching a schema. Implemented: response_mime_type=application/json plus Pydantic validation; invalid replies are rejected and nothing is saved. Temperature A model setting controlling randomness; 0 is most repeatable. Assessment uses 0; extraction uses 0.1. Untrusted-text markers Delimiters such as <untrusted_text> or <<<EVIDENCE ... EVIDENCE>>> that tell the model content is data to read, not instructions. Implemented. Marker sequences found inside input are stripped first so content cannot close a block early.

docs.title: G. Funding and nonprofit domain
docs.text:
Terms are used as KNode's data model uses them. Industry usage may treat some as interchangeable; KNode does not.

Term Definition Context in KNode Candid / ProPublica Nonprofit Explorer / GlobalGiving (IATI) Third-party sources of nonprofit profiles, financial data, and project or funder data. IATI is the International Aid Transparency Initiative data standard. Listed as organisation and registry sources in the Integrations page. Whether each is currently ingested is not established. EIN (Employer Identification Number) A nine-digit US tax identifier for an organisation. Required at sign-up for organisations, stored in organisations.ein, and the key to IRS verification (Design only). Eligibility requirement A condition an applicant must meet to be considered for an opportunity. In the data model eligibility appears twice: as structured opportunity fields (eligible geographies and organisation types, deadline) assessed by rules, and as a requirement of type eligibility assessed like any other requirement. Form 990 / 990-PF The US annual information return filed by tax-exempt organisations (990-PF for private foundations). Source of financial and geographic information (IRS data, ProPublica). Funder An organisation that provides grants. funders table and FUNDER user role. A funder owns opportunities, discovers organisations, and reviews collectives. Funding award A grant that has already been made. funding_awards. Used for historical data and the Funding Trends analysis. Not the same as an opportunity. Funding opportunity An open, upcoming or closed call to which organisations can apply. funding_opportunities. Has requirements, a deadline, a grant range and a status. Called "grant" in funder screens and "funding call" in AI prompts. Funding trends / funding landscape An analysis of historical awards by region, sector and timeframe. Implemented: POST /api/v1/trends/analysis, shown as a line chart for NGOs. Totals are reported per currency. The MVP's grant gap analysis is absent from the frontend. Grant A sum of money given for a purpose, normally without repayment. The word in funder screens for what the database calls a funding opportunity. A grant amount range is grant_min / grant_max. Grants.gov / USAspending US government sites publishing grant opportunities (Grants.gov) and historical federal awards (USAspending). Ingested as source_system values GRANTS_GOV and USASPENDING. The Grants.gov job searches for the keyword "Africa" over the last 60 days. Historical funding record A past award stored with its source. See Funding award. A missing amount or date stays empty, never zero. IRS Business Master File (BMF) / TEOS The IRS list of exempt organisations and its search service. Used to load organisations for profile building (up to 100 per run) and, by design, to verify registration. Mandatory requirement A requirement the funder marks as compulsory. is_mandatory, default true. Nonprofit organisation / NGO (non-governmental organisation) An organisation that works for public benefit, not profit, independent of government. KNode targets African-focused NGOs. The code and UI call them organisations (ORGANISATION role) and /ngo/*; the Architecture page says "NGO" and "organization". Organisation A nonprofit that seeks funding. One row in organisations, identified by a UUID. Distinct from a collective, which is a group of organisations around one opportunity. Registration in the US does not show that an organisation works in Africa. Organisation profile / organisational capability The stored description of an organisation: mission, focus areas, countries of operation and capabilities. Capabilities are the things it can do. Implemented as JSON lists on organisations. The documented assessment path reads confirmed claims and their evidence text, not these lists directly. Programme area / focus area / sector The thematic field of work. KNode uses three related words: focus_areas for organisations and funders, sector for an opportunity. AI extraction is limited to the values HEALTH and LIVELIHOODS; the database fields are free JSON. Registration status A text field on an organisation describing its legal registration. registration_status, String(100). Its allowed values are not documented. Requirement (opportunity) One condition or expectation from a funding call, stored with text, type and weight. opportunity_requirements. Types: eligibility, geography, thematic_fit, financial_capacity, partnership, evidence. At most 30 per extracted call. Verified organisation An organisation whose legal registration and domain have been checked. Design only in the Architecture page (EIN against IRS data, email domain match, OTP to a domain address, admin review). The Backend page documents only last_verified_at and an ein field.

docs.title: H. Collectives, workspaces and collaboration
docs.text:
The documentation uses collective, coalition and consortium for overlapping ideas. The data model knows only collectives. The documentation does not say whether the three words differ, so treat them as one concept until the team decides.

Term Definition Context in KNode Accepted vs proposed member Whether a collective member has accepted an invitation or is only suggested. The deterministic coverage route takes an include_proposed option, and the test plan covers accepted versus proposed members. The full status vocabulary is not documented. Coalition The funder-side word for a collective. Also in coalition_policy, a field on opportunities. Implemented in the funder UI (/funder/coalitions, lib/funderCoalitions.ts) and the API (coalition-policy). The funder list reads the same collectives records (GET /collectives?opportunity_id=). The documentation does not state this identity explicitly. Collective A group of organisations formed around one funding opportunity so that together they can meet its requirements. Implemented (collectives, collective_members). Has members, a coverage view, a lead suggestion and one workspace. Not a legal entity and not a single organisation. A collective-building match run is one of the three run types. Collective coverage (COVERED / PARTIAL / UNRESOLVED / UNCOVERED) For each requirement, whether the members together meet it. COVERED: at least one member is MET. PARTIAL: best status is PARTIALLY_MET. UNRESOLVED: no result yet and some assessments are unresolved. UNCOVERED: all relevant assessments are negative. Implemented in services/matching_engine/collective.py, plus counts of unconfirmed participants. The frontend calls the same idea capability coverage. Two coverage routes exist. Collective member / participation status A member organisation of a collective, with its response to an invitation. Implemented. Membership uniqueness and response timestamps are database constraints. The frontend tabs derive from my_membership_status (all, active, invited). Consortium The word the Architecture and Frontend pages use for the collaboration between collective members, as in "consortium workspace". Not a stored entity. There is no consortia table and no stated difference from a collective. Consortium workspace / workspace A shared work area belonging to one collective, holding workspace items. Implemented. workspaces has one row per collective; the frontend creates it on first visit (GET, then POST on 404). The word "consortium" appears only in the UI and the Frontend page. Discussion thread A conversation among collective members inside the workspace. Frontend convention only. Threads are stored as NOTE workspace items whose title starts with [t:<id>]. The backend has no thread concept. Lead organisation / lead suggestion The organisation treated as the lead when partner discovery looks for gaps; a lead suggestion proposes one for a collective. Implemented at /collectives/{id}/lead-suggestion (method and schema to be confirmed); no frontend caller. Partner discovery treats the lead's gaps as the starting point. Member invitation / respond A collective's invitation to an organisation and that organisation's reply. Implemented: POST /collectives/{id}/members/invite and .../respond. The NGO UI can accept or decline; no UI exists to send invitations (inviteMember is unused). Participation confirmed A flag stating whether a suggested partner has agreed to take part. Always false for partner suggestions. A suggestion means evidence may complement a gap, not that anyone has agreed. Referral A funder-initiated record directed to one organisation or one collective, which the recipient can respond to or the funder withdraw. Implemented in schema and routes (/referrals, respond, withdraw); no frontend caller. The Architecture page describes "funder-to-NGO interactions"; the schema also allows a collective target. Status values are not documented. Shortlist / Select Funder actions on a coalition's detail page. Placeholder: the buttons are disabled. Workspace item / task One entry in a workspace. Types seen: tasks, documents and notes. A task is an item with an assignee and status. Implemented (workspace_items). Item creation is in the NGO UI; edit and delete exist in the API but have no UI caller. Whether task status changes are supported in the UI was not traced.

docs.title: I. Data ingestion, evidence and reporting
docs.text: Term Definition Context in KNode Background job / batch job A task run outside a user request, usually on a schedule or from a command line. Implemented as Python entry points in services/jobs/ (scraper, midnight_scraper, process_grants, midnight_grants, opportunity_matching, nightly). Run by command; a production scheduler was not verified. Data ingestion / data pipeline Collecting data from outside sources, cleaning it and storing it as structured records. Implemented for Grants.gov grants, IRS organisation lists and organisation websites. Each record keeps its source and source_system. The Architecture page's queued "Data Ingestion Service" is Design only. Data validation Rejecting or cleaning data that does not meet rules. Imported data is validated and sanitised; AI output is validated against Pydantic schemas with length, number and allowed-value checks; HTML tags are stripped. Draft opportunity An AI-extracted opportunity returned for a funder to review before anything is saved. Implemented: POST /opportunities/extract (PDF, DOCX or TXT, up to 10 MB). Calls with no title, a past deadline, a non-African region or a non-open call are rejected. Email delivery (SMTP, STARTTLS) SMTP is the standard protocol for sending email; STARTTLS upgrades the connection to encrypted. Implemented in services/email_service.py on port 587 with a 15-second timeout. Used for sign-up and login codes only. In prod missing credentials raise an error; in dev the code is printed to the log. Backend settings also list Resend. Evidence ledger The frontend's name for the list of evidence entries held for an organisation. Served by GET /organisations/{id}/evidence and shown as documents (ledgerEntryToDocument). Its exact relation to sources and extracted_claims is not documented. File signature check / SHA-256 hash A file signature check compares the file's first bytes with its claimed type (%PDF, PK). A SHA-256 hash is a fingerprint that detects identical files. Implemented for uploads (PDF, DOCX, PNG). Duplicates are detected by hash. Originals are stored under a random name inside the organisation's own folder. Idempotency Repeating a request has the same effect as doing it once. Not established for matching. The Backend page lists duplicate-request and idempotency tests as outstanding. Import uniqueness on (source_system, external_id) gives it for imported records. Match report / report generation A generated document summarising matches. Not found as an exposed workflow. A reports table with JSON content exists and the Architecture page lists a Reports component that emails reports; no public report router was found. Provenance / source traceability Knowing where each fact came from and when. Implemented as a core rule. Every extracted claim links to a source; imported records keep source and retrieval date; assessments keep claim and source ids and the verified quote. Rate limiting / politeness delay Limiting how fast requests are made. Jobs pause between items (4 seconds per organisation, 7 seconds per grant). Website collection respects robots.txt. A gateway-level rate limit is Design only. Retry / backoff Repeating a failed call, waiting longer each time. Implemented for requirement assessment: up to 2 retries with exponential backoff (GEMINI_MAX_RETRIES), then ERROR. No automatic retry on the frontend, which offers manual retry on two hooks. Scraping / crawling Fetching web pages automatically and extracting content. Implemented with Requests, BeautifulSoup and Playwright. A Serper search finds an organisation's website; pages under 200 characters are discarded. Playwright here is for scraping, not testing. Source document A file or web page from which evidence was taken. Implemented as a sources row: name, URL or storage key, type, dates, content and hash. An uploaded document is kept as a source even when extraction fails. Worker / job queue A separate process that takes queued tasks so users do not wait. Design only. The Architecture page describes queued workers; the Backend page documents command-line jobs and says a scheduler is unverified.

docs.title: J. Testing and quality assurance
docs.text: Term Definition Context in KNode Contract test A test checking that two sides agree on an interface. openapiContract.test.ts checks matching endpoints and fields against the frontend's snapshot of the OpenAPI file. It does not test the live backend. Coverage (test coverage) The share of code executed by tests. Backend: pytest --cov --cov-report=term-missing. A coverage figure is not given; 71 backend files match test*.py, which is a file count, not a pass result or case count. CI (continuous integration) Automatically building and testing every change. Backend workflows ci.yml and pr-checks.yml exist. The frontend's only workflow checks that the pull-request template is ticked and does not run build, lint or tests, although its README says it does. End-to-end (E2E) test / Playwright An E2E test drives the whole app through a real browser. Playwright is a browser-automation tool. No E2E tests are documented. Playwright appears in the backend stack for scraping, not testing. Factory / fixture / mock A factory builds test records; a fixture is shared test setup; a mock replaces a real dependency. tests/factories.py, tests/conftest.py (in-memory SQLite, rollback transaction), AssessmentProvider mocked so no Gemini call is needed. Integration test A test of several parts working together, such as a route plus its database. Backend API tests use FastAPI TestClient with get_db overridden. SQLite does not prove PostgreSQL behaviour, so a separate PostgreSQL test workflow is recommended. Linting / formatting Automatic checks for code-style problems and layout. Backend: Ruff (ruff check, ruff format --check). Frontend: ESLint and Prettier, run before commits by Husky and lint-staged. pytest / Vitest The Python and JavaScript test runners. Backend uses pytest with pytest-cov. Frontend uses Vitest with jsdom and Testing Library: 10 test files. Postman An API testing tool. The docs describe importing /openapi.json and a local environment with baseUrl and accessToken. Use test accounts only. Smoke test A quick check that the main paths work after a deploy. Recommended after release: authentication, organisation and opportunity access, matching, /health. Type checking Verifying that values match declared types before running. Frontend: next build type-checks; no project script exists (npx tsc --noEmit works). Backend type checking is not documented. Unit test A test of one small function in isolation. Scoring, eligibility and quote validation are pure functions and suit unit tests.

docs.title: K. Infrastructure, deployment and operations
docs.text:
Term Definition Context in KNode CD / deployment Delivering a tested build to a running environment. Frontend hosting: Vercel. Backend: Heroku. Containers / infrastructure as code Containers package an application with its dependencies; infrastructure as code defines servers and networks in files. Design only (Architecture). Development / test / staging / production Environments of increasing realism and risk. The ENV setting accepts dev, test, staging, prod. Dev prints one-time codes to logs; prod requires SMTP credentials. Health check An endpoint that reports whether the service is up. GET /health returns {"status":"ok"}. It is a constant and not a database or provider readiness check. Logging / monitoring Logging records events; monitoring watches metrics and alerts. Logging Implemented via configure_logging (DEBUG in dev, INFO otherwise). Metrics, tracing, alerting and log aggregation were not verified. MkDocs A static-site generator for documentation. Builds this documentation site (Material theme), deployed from GitHub Actions to GitHub Pages. Object storage / pre-signed URL Cloud file storage; a pre-signed URL is a time-limited link to one file. Design only. Current uploads are stored in a local UPLOAD_DIR. Release step (migrations) Applying database migrations deliberately when releasing. Recommended: run Alembic as a controlled release step, confirm /health, smoke-test, then schedule jobs only if intended. Secrets manager A service that stores secrets and hands them to applications. ## Acronym and abbreviation index

Only abbreviations that appear in the documentation are listed. ERD and PRD do not appear in any page provided. Where a concept has a master-glossary entry, the entry holds the full definition; this table gives the expansion and one line of use.

Abbreviation Full form Meaning or use in KNode AI Artificial intelligence Gemini-based extraction and requirement assessment. See section F. API Application Programming Interface The backend's JSON endpoints under /api/v1. ARIA Accessible Rich Internet Applications aria-* attributes used in the sidebar drawer, tabs and alerts. BMF Business Master File IRS list of exempt organisations used to seed organisations. CD Continuous deployment Delivering tested builds automatically. See section K. CI Continuous integration Automated build and test on each change. See section J. CORS Cross-Origin Resource Sharing CORS_ALLOW_ORIGINS allow-list. CRUD Create, Read, Update, Delete Basic data operations on most entities. CSP Content Security Policy Not set by the frontend; noted as a gap. CSR Client-side rendering How almost all frontend pages render. DDoS Distributed denial of service Perimeter protection in the security design . DKIM / DMARC / SPF Email authentication standards Email sender protection . DSN Data source name The database connection string form of DATABASE_URL. E2E End-to-end No E2E tests documented. EIN Employer Identification Number US tax id on organisations.ein. GCP Google Cloud Platform GCP_PROJECT_ID and GCP_REGION for the Vertex AI fallback. GUID / UUID Globally / Universally Unique Identifier Primary key type. HSTS HTTP Strict Transport Security Forces HTTPS . HTTP / HTTPS Hypertext Transfer Protocol (Secure) Transport for the API. IaC Infrastructure as code Design only. IATI International Aid Transparency Initiative Data standard used by GlobalGiving. IRS Internal Revenue Service (US) Source of exempt-organisation data. JSON JavaScript Object Notation Request, response and column format. JTI JWT ID Per-token id used for revocation. JWT JSON Web Token Access and refresh tokens. KMS Key Management Service Design only. LLM Large language model Gemini. MFA Multi-factor authentication The frontend reads an mfa_required flag from the login response; the second factor is the emailed OTP. MIME Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions Media type, for example application/json or supported upload types. MVP Minimum viable product The scope document referenced by the Frontend page; not provided. NGO Non-governmental organisation The product's primary user. ORM Object-Relational Mapping SQLAlchemy. OTP One-time password Six-digit emailed code for sign-up and login. RBAC Role-Based Access Control Role dependencies in the backend. REST Representational State Transfer The API style. RLS Row-Level Security Design only. SAD / SSAD System Architecture Diagram / Security System Architecture Diagram Figures 1 and 2 in the Architecture page. SDK Software development kit Google Gen AI SDK used for Gemini. SMTP Simple Mail Transfer Protocol Email delivery. SQL Structured Query Language Database query language. SSE-KMS Server-side encryption with KMS keys Design only. SSRF Server-side request forgery Ingestion protection (Design only). TEOS Tax Exempt Organization Search IRS search service. TLS Transport Layer Security Encrypted connections. TOTP Time-based one-time password Design only, funders and admins. TTL Time to live Lifetime in seconds of tokens and OTPs. UI User interface The Next.js frontend. WAF Web application firewall Design only. WCAG Web Content Accessibility Guidelines The Frontend page states conformance is not claimed. XSS Cross-site scripting Risk noted for tokens in sessionStorage.

docs.title: Integrations
docs.text: KNode connects to a small set of third-party services. This page describes each one: what it does, what data it handles, how it is configured, and how the system behaves when it is unavailable.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Integration Purpose in KNode Google Gemini Reads uploaded documents and extracts structured facts about an organisation Email (SMTP) Delivers sign-up and login verification codes PostgreSQL Stores all application data Funding data: USAspending and Grants.gov Supplies historical awards and funding opportunities Organisation and registry sources Builds organisation profiles from public information Uploaded documents Evidence supplied directly by organisations

docs.title: How the integrations fit together
docs.text:
┌───────────────────────────┐
  Browser ──────────▶ │  Next.js frontend         │
  (NGO / Funder)      └─────────────┬─────────────┘
                                    │  HTTPS, JWT, /api/v1/*
                                    ▼
                      ┌───────────────────────────┐
                      │  FastAPI backend          │
                      └───┬───────────┬───────┬───┘
                          │           │       │
              ┌───────────▼──┐  ┌─────▼────┐  ┌▼─────────────────┐
              │ PostgreSQL   │  │ SMTP     │  │ Google Gemini    │
              │ (data)       │  │ (email)  │  │ (extraction)     │
              └──────▲───────┘  └──────────┘  └──────────────────┘
                     │
        USAspending · Grants.gov · IRS · ProPublica ·
        Candid · GlobalGiving · organisation websites

Every integration sits behind the backend. The frontend never calls a third party directly, and no third-party key is ever sent to the browser.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: When an organisation uploads a report, Gemini reads it and returns structured facts: mission, focus areas, countries of operation, capabilities, annual revenue, registration status and headline impact metrics. The backend stores these facts as claims in the organisation's evidence ledger.

docs.title: Flow
docs.text:
1. The user uploads a PDF, DOCX or PNG to POST /api/v1/organisations/{id}/documents.
  2. The backend checks the file type, size and file signature, then stores the file.
  3. services/document_extraction.py sends the document to Gemini with a fixed instruction prompt and a JSON schema describing the expected answer.
  4. The response is validated again in the backend against the ExtractedProfile model.
  5. Each extracted fact is saved as a PENDING claim linked to its source document. A person must confirm a claim before it counts as verified.

docs.title: Data sent to Gemini
docs.text: Sent Never sent The document content (PDF and PNG as files, DOCX as extracted text capped at 100,000 characters) Account details, passwords or tokens The fixed instruction prompt Other organisations' data The JSON schema for the answer Database records

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: Setting Meaning GEMINI_API_KEY API key for Gemini. Without it, the upload API answers 503 AI_NOT_CONFIGURED. GEMINI_MODEL Gemini model used for extraction MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES Largest file accepted UPLOAD_DIR Folder where uploaded files are stored

docs.title: Safeguards
docs.text:
• Untrusted input. The prompt instructs the model to treat the document as data and ignore any instructions written inside it.
  • Structured output. The model must answer in JSON that matches the schema. The backend validates the result again, because the model does not enforce length and pattern limits.
  • No guessing. The model uses only what the document states and leaves unknown fields empty.
  • Human review. Extracted facts remain PENDING until a person confirms them.
  • Additive only. Extraction adds claims. It never overwrites what an organisation or an administrator has entered.
  • Private logs. Failures log the type of error only, never document text.

docs.title: Failure behaviour
docs.text:
Situation API response No API key configured 503 with code AI_NOT_CONFIGURED Network error, quota exceeded or unreadable file 502 with code EXTRACTION_FAILED Model output does not match the schema 502 with code EXTRACTION_FAILED

The uploaded document is kept as a source in every case, so a failed extraction never loses the file.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
KNode sends one-time codes by email for two purposes:

Purpose When it is sent Sign-up verification After registration, to activate the account Login verification After a correct email and password, to complete login

Codes have six digits, expire after 10 minutes (OTP_TTL_SECONDS) and allow five attempts (OTP_MAX_ATTEMPTS). Codes are stored hashed.

docs.text: ENV When SMTP credentials are not set dev, test, staging The email is skipped and a warning is logged. In dev the one-time code is printed in the server log. prod Sending raises an error. Credentials are mandatory.

docs.title: Design
docs.text:
• Emails use a branded HTML template with a plain-text fallback.
  • Messages contain the code and the recipient's name only.
  • Connections use TLS and a 15 second timeout.

docs.title: PostgreSQL
docs.text:
PostgreSQL is the system of record. It holds users, organisations, funders, sources and claims, funding opportunities and awards, matches, collectives, workspaces, referrals, reports and audit events.

Setting Meaning DATABASE_URL PostgreSQL connection string (required)

All schema changes go through Alembic migrations. See the Backend page for the migration workflow.

docs.title: Funding data sources
docs.text:
Historical awards power the Funding Trends dashboard, and open calls power opportunity search. Every record stores where it came from, so any figure can be traced to its source.

Source Provides Recorded as USAspending.gov Historical awards source_system = 'USASPENDING' Grants.gov Opportunities and awards source_system = 'GRANTS_GOV' Web crawler Opportunities and awards from funder sites source_system = 'CRAWLER' Manual entry Opportunities added by a funder or administrator source_system = 'MANUAL'

docs.title: Data integrity rules
docs.text:
• Every award links to a source record, and (source_system, external_id) is unique, so the same award can never be stored twice.
  • A missing amount or date stays empty. It is never stored as zero.
  • Currencies are never mixed. The trends API reports totals per currency.
  • Corrections to an award require a reason, and each correction is written to the audit log.

docs.title: Organisation and registry sources
docs.text:
Organisation profiles are built from public information. Each fact keeps a link to its source and the date it was retrieved.

Source Provides IRS Business Master File (BMF) Registration and tax-exempt status IRS Tax Exempt Organization Search (TEOS) Status of US tax-exempt organisations IRS Form 990 and 990-PF filings Financial information ProPublica Nonprofit Explorer Organisation financial data Candid Organisation profile data GlobalGiving and GlobalGiving IATI Projects, opportunities and funder data Organisation websites and published reports Programmes, impact and evidence

docs.title: Rules that apply to every source
docs.text:
• Imported data is validated and sanitised before it is stored.
  • US registration or tax-exempt status alone does not show that an organisation works in Africa. Evidence of operations comes from programme descriptions, project records, filings or reports.
  • Personal contact details are not collected beyond an organisation's published contact point.
  • Collection from websites respects robots.txt and site terms, and is rate limited.
  • Imported data extends a profile. It never overwrites what an organisation has claimed.

docs.title: Uploaded documents
docs.text:
Organisations can upload impact reports and similar documents as evidence.

Item Rule Accepted types PDF, DOCX and PNG Validation The file extension and the file signature must match (%PDF for PDF, PK for DOCX). Size is capped by MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES. Duplicates A SHA-256 hash detects the same file uploaded twice File names The original name is sanitised for display. Files are stored under a random name inside the organisation's own folder. Visibility Only the owning organisation's members and administrators can see an uploaded document Audit Every upload is written to the audit log Storage UPLOAD_DIR

The Next.js frontend talks only to the KNode backend, through the versioned /api/v1 prefix.

docs.text:
1. Email. Leave SMTP_USER empty with ENV=dev, register a user, and read the code from the server log. To test real delivery, set the SMTP_* values with a Gmail app password.
